name: Raffles Medical
summary: Islandwide clinic network many expats use for GP, health screening, paediatric panels, and first-stop private care — confirm mental-health and dental carve-outs separately; ask for workplace-injury documentation when relevant.
body: Raffles Medical clinics are a common first GP relationship for newcomers who want English-first private care and islandwide coverage. Before you attach, confirm your employer insurer’s panel list, nearest clinic hours to home and office, and what to do after 10pm — clinic networks are not a substitute for knowing your closest appropriate A&E. Families often use the network for paediatric acute visits when panel rates apply; still keep a named paediatrician relationship if you want continuity. National Childhood Immunisation Schedule catch-up for foreign kids usually still needs NIR record upload before polyclinic continuity — private panels help for fever but do not replace registry and diphtheria/measles pass paperwork. For elective hospital admissions, ask HR for the Letter of Guarantee workflow early — foreigners without MediSave commonly face large admission deposits without an LOG. If the injury arose at work, tell the clinician it is a workplace injury, keep Singapore-issued MCs and bills, and notify HR the same day — EP holders remain covered under WICA even when mandatory WIC insurance does not apply to high-salary non-manual roles. Capacity planning (LPA Certificate Issuer visits, AMD with a doctor) can start at a familiar GP once you understand Form 1 vs Form 2 fees for PRs and foreigners. Mental-health outpatient (psychology / counselling) and dental are frequently excluded or capped on basic corporate riders — ask HR for the benefits schedule before you assume sessions or scaling are reimbursable. Fertility investigations may start at a GP panel, but MOH ART co-funding is citizenship-gated at public AR centres — EP–EP couples should budget cash rates and not assume MediSave. If you arrived with controlled ADHD / anxiety meds under HSA approval, book a GP or specialist early so your local prescription path is ready before the import supply ends. Pair with the healthcare, dental, personal-medication, paediatrician, childhood-vaccination, newborn-pass, IVF, LPA/AMD, WICA, and mental-health guides for triage. Ask whether physiotherapy, sports-medicine, and optical services sit inside the same panel billing rules as GP visits — allied-health and spectacle benefits are frequently capped or excluded even when the clinic logo matches your insurer brochure. Older visiting parents on Social Visit/LTVP often need a named GP plan mid-stay — pair clinical continuity with the grandparents long-stay caregiving guide. Family ops note: dengue-season child fevers need same-day GP paths and a named coverage adult — forum platelet folklore is not a care plan. Family ops: red-eye / sticky-eye mornings still need a named coverage owner before the school bus decision. Family ops: impetigo / crusty-sore mornings still need a named coverage owner before the school-bus decision.
